Figure 8: BESS Demand Response at USU Microgrid Facility The USU microgrid system accepts OpenADR signals for the BESS for external load dispatches from the endpoint manager. With the large battery the USU microgrid is capable of becoming a temporary load to store excess energy in conjunction with curtailment of solar. During Budget Period 2, the BESS vendor introduced a load reduction capability to meet UDERMS requirements. The figure below illustrates these two outcomes using sample BESS data from Soleil Lofts. The top panel shows PV production (yellow) alongside battery charging (green) and discharging (red). The middle panel displays total residential consumption, while the bottom panel compares grid imports (purple) with grid exports (blue). A frequency response event is visible as a short export spike (about 60 seconds) near 12 PM. Load reduction is demonstrated by contrasting residential consumption with grid imports: between 9 AM and 11:59 PM, grid demand is reduced as on-site load is served by PV generation and stored battery energy. Building on this foundation, UDERMS is contributing to the advancement of the Wattsmart program by enabling discussion and testing of additional grid services on devices enrolled at Soleil Lofts and Citizens West. 27 Figure 9: Soliel Lofts BESS Frequency Response and Load Reduction 6.1.8.3.1.5 Electric Vehicles EV load is managed by using OCPP 1.6 to send curtailment commands to vehicle chargers. The curtailment commands contain a charge profile that specifies the intended shape of power draw, as well as the duration for which the command is valid. After the command has expired the charger will fall back to a default charge profile, or to normal free charging. Charge profiles may be set beforehand and last indefinitely, or they may be sent during a charge session to dynamically impact charging behavior. The OCPP protocol provides semantic control interface to the chargers which allows inner complexity to be managed by the charger itself. The USU microgrid facility uses the default profile to set a hard limit on how much power can be pulled on any given day. When vehicles are charging, in-session curtailments are used during the peak shaving process to reduce the load of the facility during times of low solar, or otherwise high facility power usage. 28 6.1.8.3.1.6 Solar Figure 10: USU Microgrid Facility Solar Power Usage At the USU microgrid, the solar is used to load shift and peak shave in conjunction with the battery.
